_timing: No narration yet. Each beat is the larger of the time it needs to finish animating and the time it takes to read, plus a 22-frame hold. This is a floor, not considered pacing — measure a real read and switch this topic to voiceCuts.

beats.text: Pixar nearly lost Toy Story 2 to one command.
beats.note: The Unix command was rm -r -f, which deletes everything below a folder without asking.

beats.context: Of the film files were gone. The directory had shrunk to a tenth of its expected size.

beats.text: The film was then largely rebuilt anyway.
beats.note: After Christmas 1998 most animation, layout, lighting and effects were redone, with release locked for 22 November 1999.

beats.name: Galyn Susman
beats.role: Supervising technical director. She had been working from home after having a baby, so her workstation held a recent copy.

beats.text: They carried the workstation to the studio in a car.
beats.note: Susman and Oren Jacob moved it wrapped in blankets. The team then checked about 30,000 files against older archives.

beats.text: The film was saved by a baby.

beats.line: Tech has a habit of nearly breaking.
